title: NPER error lane: 7 of 7 typed-error rows matched, on the structural axis
upstream_status_verbatim: identified and signed off `1286/1286` + `7/7` error rows (catalogue reconcile 2026-07-11; the G6-08 row was removed)
status_plain: Seven of NPER's rows are typed error results rather than numbers, and the production kernel matched Excel on all seven. Matching an error placement is the structural-admission axis by the honesty spine's own definition, not the numeric-bits axis, so this count is recorded here and not beside the 1,286 numeric rows. The repair the seven rows pin is a real behavioural change: NPER(0, 0, ..) publishes #DIV/0! where OxFunc previously published #NUM!. Recording these seven rows on the numeric axis, as the earlier harvest did by adding them to 1,286, both fabricates a figure and leaves NPER reading as having no structural comparison record when it holds an error-lane sign-off.

counts.build_note: The document's section header at line 8 names "live Excel 16.0 build 20131, x86-64" but governs a different section; this figure sits under "## Sign-off" and restates no build. Not inherited.
counts.corpus_or_build: the typed-error rows among every deduplicated answered NPER witness, replayed by `calc_graph_racer verify_nper_promotion`
counts.ambiguity_note: Seven rows is a very small structural corpus. "7 of 7" here means the error CODE and its placement matched, which is a different predicate in spirit from bit equality even though the comparison is exact. The source does not enumerate all seven; one is named: "- `NPER(0, 0, ..)` publishes `#DIV/0!` (OxFunc previously `#NUM!`)."
